doc: The OpenAI Codex CLI's `[otel]` telemetry. Its spans are its own `tracing` instrumentation - hundreds per turn, none in the GenAI conventions, none carrying text - so the conversation is entirely in its log events: the prompt (`log_user_prompt`), each tool call with its arguments and output, and the reply (`log_agent_responses`). A record names a span only while the trace exporter runs; that is what joins it to a turn, and with logs alone nothing can. The model's reasoning is never exported, and nor is the system prompt.

carriers.doc: The user's turn, or a sub-agent's task, once per turn. A snapshot, the cautious reading the resolver gives a carrier nobody classified: one record per turn or call, so it can neither invent a duplicate nor need the stronger guarantees of an emission.

The call, rebuilt from the record of its result. A snapshot, the cautious reading the resolver gives a carrier nobody classified: one record per turn or call, so it can neither invent a duplicate nor need the stronger guarantees of an emission.

What the tool returned. A snapshot, the cautious reading the resolver gives a carrier nobody classified: one record per turn or call, so it can neither invent a duplicate nor need the stronger guarantees of an emission.

A turn's final reply. A snapshot, the cautious reading the resolver gives a carrier nobody classified: one record per turn or call, so it can neither invent a duplicate nor need the stronger guarantees of an emission.

detect.doc: Codex names its service after the client that runs it: `codex_exec` for `codex exec`, `codex_cli_rs` for the interactive CLI, `codex_vscode` for the editor extension.
detect.label: Codex

message_events.name: codex.user_prompt
message_events.doc: The user's prompt, or a sub-agent's task. A container: `prompt` is the turn.

message_events.name: codex.agent_response
message_events.doc: The agent's reply at the end of a turn; `agent.type` says whether the main agent or a sub-agent gave it.

message_events.name: codex.tool_result
message_events.doc: One finished tool call: its name, call id, arguments and output on one record.

log_events.name: codex.user_prompt
log_events.doc: Named by the `event.name` attribute only: the record's own event name is the `tracing` call site (`event otel/src/events/session_telemetry.rs:1150`), which the OpenTelemetry bridge writes there.

messages.doc: The user's turn. Without `log_user_prompt` the record carries a redaction marker, which is read as what it says.
The call, from the record of its result: the model's arguments are kept verbatim there.
What the tool returned, answering its call. A shell command's output includes Codex's own header (chunk id, wall time, exit code), which is what the model read.
